issue: PMAT-564 (forjar#564; paiml/infra#605 first signature) — `forjar drift -f forjar-ephemeral.yaml` on yoga inspected 0 of the 10 resources that manifest declares, graded two files from forjar.yaml (a manifest it was not given, in a category its own census called skipped), printed `Drift detected: 2 resource(s)` and exited 0. Now a run that inspected none of its declared resources declines with exit 2 and names the count, and no detector grades a locked resource the config does not declare.
recorded_at: stacked on PMAT-562 (PR #563) — the diff against main includes that branch; re-bound when this branch is rebased onto the squash-merged #563

quorum.rounds: one round of three sandboxed agy quorum lanes against self-contained clones of the PR worktree at bd1664a8, diffed against the base branch PMAT-562-drift-exits-on-drift, --not-before pinned, out_dir keyed by ticket AND session id; lane-reduce agreed=false (2 PASS / 1 FAIL), partial_reasons recording two lanes sharing a model id
quorum.kill_rule: the FAIL lane's image-detector finding was confirmed by reading image.rs (the other two lanes never opened it) and fixed with a unit test that fails without the guard; the point two resampled lanes agreed on and got wrong (expansion timing) was settled by reading load_drift_config; five mutations were run against the committed tree
refuted_claims: That a locked resource the config does not declare is skipped as not-in-config by every detector. The image detector walked the lock with no config check, and census.inspected overwrites a skip, so it could grade another manifest's image. Guarded, with a unit test.
That N counts count:/for_each: resources pre-expansion (two lanes sharing a model id). load_drift_config calls parse_and_validate, which expands them before cmd_drift sees the config.

That the first cut of the decline was correct. It declined over an unreachable host and turned two FALSIFY-549 cases red (exit 2 for 4); the unmeasured guard fixed it and the cases went green untouched.
That every lane left its clone byte-identical. Lane 1 wrote a three-line file into its own clone; agy-lane.sh kept the clone and said so; the shared checkout was clean.
lane_errors: lane 1 wrote test_image_skip.rs into its own sandbox clone despite a NO WRITES brief (KEPT, isolation held)
the delegate's dispatch-local model config first matched fanout.sh's lane-*.json glob (children=4) and was renamed before lane-reduce ran

falsification.test: six cases through the binary with two manifests on one machine: the decline with its count; another manifest's tampered file never graded; the census never both inspects and skips a locked, undeclared resource; a partially locked manifest is graded, not declined, and its drift is a reject; the applied manifest is fully inspected; --json declines with the same code. Plus a unit case that an undeclared locked image is skipped as not-in-config, and three older cases inverted from exit 0 over 'inspected 0 of N' to the decline they described.
falsification.reverted: five mutations over the COMMITTED tree, each restored from HEAD. M1 deletes the decline call: the regression and --json cases red. M2 passes declared_only=false: 5 of 6 red. M3 drops the unmeasured guard: two FALSIFY-549 cases red with exit 2 for 4. M4 declines whenever declared > 0: the partially-locked control and the applied manifest red. M5 drops the image detector's config guard: its unit case red. `git status --porcelain` empty after each.
falsification.observed_failure: inspected 2 of 103 … declared here, absent from the lock 10 … DRIFTED: gitconfig on yoga … Drift detected: 2 resource(s), rc=0 — forjar 1.30.0 on yoga, 2026-09-15 11:51Z; reproduced with two local manifests: RED 5 of 6 with src/ reverted under the test file
falsification.still_green_when_reverted: the drift suites this repository already had — scopes_to_the_config_it_was_given, measures_a_broken_guard, apply_sees_the_target_file, ignore_drift_names_one_field, e05 — and the workspace

systems: Terraform (a plan is drawn only against the state its backend holds for that configuration)
Ansible (a play matching no hosts skips and exits 0 unless fail_on_no_hosts — the fail-open default removed here)
Kubernetes (`kubectl diff` over absent objects shows creations in the manifest's own namespace, never another's)
Nix (an attribute that names nothing is an error, not a successful build of nothing)
crux.verdict: accept(three of four surveyed systems key a comparison to what it was asked about and refuse an empty question; Ansible is the fail-open counterexample. forjar's defect was worse than Ansible's — it did not merely skip, it graded another manifest's resources under this one's name. Where forjar remains weaker: `--dry-run` previews with nothing inspected and exits 0, by design, since a preview has no verdict to give.)
